move: browser windows slide into a 3D depth stack, headlines rise, fly out
how: Three 660x420 browser mockups sit in a wrapper pre-rotated rotateY -14 / rotateX 6 with posed depth offsets (z 0, -300, -600; rotateY 0, -8, -14). Back to front, each fromTo's x from +700 with opacity 0 to its pose over 1.1s expo.out, staggered 0.25s in the first 25% of the 7s duration; after each lands its headline lines rise from yPercent 110 inside overflow-hidden spans (0.08s stagger, expo.out), paragraph and CTAs fade up (power3.out) and three colour cards rise with back.out(1.5). From 21% the whole wrapper pans rotateY -14->-6, x -80->0 over 4s sine.inOut while each page scrolls y -150 then back (power3.inOut) around 46-86%. At 89% windows fly to x -900 with opacity 0 (expo.in) front to back, and the credit fades.
adapt: Replace the three site records (url, name, accent, two-line headline, three card colours, dark flag) and the credit line; the pose array sets the stack spacing. Keep the 1.1s expo.out entries with 0.25s stagger and the 4s sine pan.
port: mount(el, shot) builds .wrap with the windows from shot.sites and applies the initial gsap.set on the wrapper; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at (0.014 + k*0.036)*D, pan at 0.21D, scrolls at 0.46D/0.7D and exit at 0.886D. The stage supplies perspective:1800px so el must carry it; the poses assume a 1280x720 frame.
caveats: from() tweens on headline/paragraph/cards without immediateRender:false
loop does not close: windows fly out left
